subject.title: fix(security): bound plugin manifest reads in audit deep scan

question: Should OpenClaw define 1 MiB as a canonical plugin-manifest limit across loading and audit, or may deep audit alone warn and skip entrypoint extraction for larger otherwise accepted manifests?
rationale: The patch safely bounds memory use, but the permanent size limit and the behavior when entrypoint extraction is skipped define security coverage and compatibility policy that automation cannot choose.

options.title: Align all manifest readers
options.body: Make the size limit or canonical bounded parser apply consistently to install, runtime loading, and audit so accepted plugins cannot exceed the audit contract.

options.title: Accept audit-only cutoff
options.body: Keep this patch as written only after a security owner explicitly accepts warning-and-skip behavior and confirms deep scanning remains adequate.

options.title: Pause for registry integration
options.body: Hold the PR until audit can consume already-resolved canonical plugin entrypoints instead of reparsing package.json independently.

recommendation.title: Align all manifest readers
recommendation.body: Make the size limit or canonical bounded parser apply consistently to install, runtime loading, and audit so accepted plugins cannot exceed the audit contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Core security-boundary policy and recent repository security work make this the strongest available decision-owner signal.
